body:
First of all, you shouldn never invoke other beans in a `@PreDestroy` callback, especially beans with the same scope. The reason is that (1) ordering is not defined; so `MyAPIClient` could have been destroyed before `autoLogout()` is called and thus a new `MyAPIClient` bean instance could be created (and this may or may not cause all kind of issues),  and (2) the context of the other bean may not be active at all.

Now, you're right that in this particular case, the `ContextNotActiveException` does not make sense since both `MyAPIClient` and `SessionManager` are `@SessionScoped`. However, we'll need more info - a full stack trace and ideally a simple reproducer app.

BTW `@SessionScoped` is not supported by default, unless the `quarkus-undertow`  extension is used. Is it the case?

Many thanks @mkouba for your rapid feedback.

Your recommendation refers to ARC specifically or is this best practice for CDI in general?  

In **Wildfly/Weld** this never was a problem.

OK. I'll try to provide a small reproducer during the next days.


> BTW `@SessionScoped` is not supported by default, unless the `quarkus-undertow` extension is used. Is it the case?

Yes, of course. I'm using myfaces-quarkus that has quarkus-undertow as a dependency. I'm trying to migrate an older JSF app from Wildfly. It went quite smooth and the mentioned issue was the only considerable obstacle until now.

I'm aware that this kind of use is not the one Quarkus was invented for and the use of @SessionScope is somewhat old-school. However there may be others trying the migration of older webapps.

> Your recommendation refers to ARC specifically or is this best practice for CDI in general?

For CDI in general. CC @manovotn 

> OK. I'll try to provide a small reproducer during the next days.

+1

Here you can find a small reproducer app:

https://github.com/miguelzapaton/quarkus-predestroy-reproducer

It confirms the described behaviour. 

For my issue I already have a workaround in mind. 

However this could be of general interest as the code worked perfectly in Weld before.

I can see the problem now. The `HttpSession` is invalidated due to a timeout, i.e. the context is destroyed in a `HttpSessionListener#sessionDestroyed()` callback. However, no `HttpServletRequest` available at this point (obviously) and the `io.quarkus.undertow.runtime.HttpSessionContext` does not support this use case and thus a client proxy invocation fails.

We'll need to modify the `HttpSessionContext` to support this use case.

issue.title: Undertow - fix CDI session context
issue.body:
- make it possible to call other session scoped beans in a pre-destroy callback; note that it's not recommended but it's not forbidden either
- resolves #29783

body:
> > OK. Later I'll add a manual session.invalidate() action to the reproducer to check what happens ...
> 
> Manual session invalidation works in different scenarios - see updated reproducer.

Yes, that's expected. [This pull request](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/29832) should fix the problem. However, keep in mind that if a `@SessionScoped` bean is created during the destruction of the context then it might not be destroyed correctly, i.e. its `@PreDestroy` callback is not invoked.

> Your recommendation refers to ARC specifically or is this best practice for CDI in general?

This is true for CDI in general, even for Weld.
Martin is right that specification doesn't give any guarantees in this regard.

The fact that it works in Weld is probably because we already encountered it at some point and did a best effort approach that works at least for some scenarios.
